title: 计算机科学，从零搭建 · 第27部分：证明与随机性

chapters.Frontier: 15. 前沿：MIP* = RE 与实践中的证明
chapters.Outro: 回顾、习题，以及它们会在哪里再出现

50fc74979956.en: A proof used to mean a document you read from beginning to end. This part breaks that idea three ways. <bookmark mark='a'/> First: a proof can be written so that reading a handful of random bits of it is enough. A correct proof always passes; any proof of a false statement is caught with high probability. <bookmark mark='b'/> Second: a proof can be a conversation. A prover claims a formula has seven satisfying assignments. We ask random questions, and a lying prover survives about one time in five when we work modulo ninety-seven, and never in our trials with a field of a million elements. <bookmark mark='c'/> Third: a proof can reveal nothing except that the statement is true. You can be convinced that a graph has a three-colouring without learning anything about it; a cheater has less than a one in a billion chance of surviving three hundred rounds. <bookmark mark='d'/> Each trades certainty for a chance of error, and the chance can be made as small as we like.
50fc74979956.zh: 证明，过去指的是一份从头读到尾的文件。这一部分从三个方向打破这个观念。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一：证明可以写成这样一种形式，只读其中随机的几位就够了。正确的证明总能通过；而一个假命题的任何证明，都会以很高的概率被识破。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二：证明可以是一场对话。一个证明者声称某个公式有七个满足赋值。我们随机提问，在模九十七下运算时，撒谎的证明者大约五次能蒙混过关一次；而在一百万元素的域上，我们的试验中一次也没有。<bookmark mark='c'/>第三：证明可以除了命题为真之外什么也不泄露。你可以相信一个图能三着色，却对它一无所知；作弊者撑过三百轮的机会不到十亿分之一。<bookmark mark='d'/>每一种都用确定性换来一个出错的机会，而这个机会可以要多小就有多小。

1ee7cde592b7.en: Part 27 of Computer Science, Built: Proofs and Randomness. <bookmark mark='a'/> In this part: the complexity classes of randomized algorithms, and why randomness may not add power after all; lower bounds for circuits, including the switching lemma, which we measure; communication between two parties; interactive proofs, from graph non-isomorphism to the sum-check protocol and IP equals PSPACE; zero knowledge; the PCP theorem, and why it makes approximation hard; the Unique Games Conjecture; fine-grained and parameterized complexity; counting; and a 2020 result connecting proofs with quantum entanglement and the halting problem.
1ee7cde592b7.zh: 计算机科学，从零搭建，第27部分：证明与随机性。<bookmark mark='a'/>这一部分包括：随机算法的复杂性类，以及为什么随机性也许终究不增加能力；电路下界，包括我们亲手测量的切换引理；双方之间的通信；交互式证明，从图非同构到 sum-check 协议与 IP 等于 PSPACE；零知识；PCP 定理，以及它为什么让近似变难；唯一博弈猜想；细粒度复杂性与参数化复杂性；计数；还有2020年一个把证明与量子纠缠和停机问题联系起来的结果。

10063fb712d8.en: Part 20 used coins to make algorithms simpler and faster. Here are the classes they define, named by John Gill in 1977. <bookmark mark='a'/> RP allows one-sided error: never a false yes, and a true yes at least half the time. Compositeness is the classic example, with the Miller-Rabin test. <bookmark mark='b'/> coRP is the mirror image. <bookmark mark='c'/> ZPP never errs, but its running time is a random variable, like quicksort with random pivots. <bookmark mark='d'/> And BPP allows error on both sides, at most a third, on every input. <bookmark mark='e'/> They nest: P inside ZPP, which is exactly RP intersect coRP, inside BPP, inside polynomial space. <bookmark mark='f'/> Notice that the probability is over the algorithm's coins. The input is arbitrary, even chosen by an adversary.
10063fb712d8.zh: 第20部分用硬币让算法更简单、更快。这里是它们所定义的类，由 John Gill 在1977年命名。<bookmark mark='a'/>RP 允许单侧错误：从不错说“是”，而真正的“是”至少有一半的时候被说出。合数判定是经典例子，用的是 Miller-Rabin 测试。<bookmark mark='b'/>coRP 是它的镜像。<bookmark mark='c'/>ZPP 从不出错，但运行时间是随机变量，就像随机选枢轴的快速排序。<bookmark mark='d'/>而 BPP 允许两侧都出错，在每个输入上至多三分之一。<bookmark mark='e'/>它们层层嵌套：P 在 ZPP 之内，ZPP 恰好等于 RP 与 coRP 的交，它又在 BPP 之内，BPP 在多项式空间之内。<bookmark mark='f'/>注意，概率是对算法自己的硬币而言的。输入是任意的，甚至可以由对手挑选。

02b3feaafeb5.en: Why a third? Any constant below a half would do, because errors can be driven down. <bookmark mark='a'/> Run the algorithm k times with fresh coins and take the majority answer. <bookmark mark='b'/> The majority is wrong only if more than half of the runs are. We computed the exact binomial tail: a hundred and one runs bring the error from a third to under three in ten thousand; two hundred and one runs, to about one in two million. <bookmark mark='c'/> The Chernoff bound, from the tail bounds of AI, Built, guarantees exponential decay in k. <bookmark mark='d'/> So the threshold of a third is arbitrary: any error bounded away from a half defines the same class.
02b3feaafeb5.zh: 为什么是三分之一？任何小于二分之一的常数都行，因为错误可以压下去。<bookmark mark='a'/>用新的硬币把算法运行 k 次，取多数答案。<bookmark mark='b'/>只有超过一半的运行出错，多数才会出错。我们计算了精确的二项式尾部：一百零一次运行把错误从三分之一降到万分之三以下；两百零一次，降到大约两百万分之一。<bookmark mark='c'/>人工智能，从零搭建中的尾部界，Chernoff 界，保证了随 k 指数衰减。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以三分之一这个门槛是任意的：任何与二分之一保持距离的错误率，都定义同一个类。

dc2fcde4bb7f.en: Amplification has a surprising consequence. <bookmark mark='a'/> Amplify until the error on each input is below two to the minus n plus one: for inputs of a hundred bits, about eleven hundred runs. <bookmark mark='b'/> There are two to the n inputs of length n, so the probability that a random string of coins is bad for any of them is at most two to the n times the error: below a half. <bookmark mark='c'/> So some single string of coins is good for every input of that length. <bookmark mark='d'/> Build it into the circuit, and the randomness disappears: one polynomial-size circuit per input length. Leonard Adleman proved this in 1978. <bookmark mark='e'/> And Michael Sipser, Péter Gács and Clemens Lautemann showed that BPP sits in the second level of the polynomial hierarchy of Part 26.
dc2fcde4bb7f.zh: 放大有一个出人意料的推论。<bookmark mark='a'/>一直放大，直到每个输入上的错误低于二的负 n 加一次方：对一百位的输入，大约一千一百次运行。<bookmark mark='b'/>长度为 n 的输入有二的 n 次方个，所以一串随机硬币对其中任何一个是坏的概率，至多是二的 n 次方乘以错误率：低于一半。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以存在某一串硬币，对这个长度的每个输入都是好的。<bookmark mark='d'/>把它固化进电路，随机性就消失了：每个输入长度一个多项式规模的电路。Leonard Adleman 在1978年证明了这一点。<bookmark mark='e'/>而 Michael Sipser、Péter Gács 和 Clemens Lautemann 证明了，BPP 位于第26部分多项式层级的第二层。

78c845123259.en: Part 20's frontier previewed the idea; here is how it works. <bookmark mark='a'/> Start with a short truly random seed, only logarithmically many bits. Choose many subsets of its positions that overlap very little, a combinatorial design, and apply a hard function f to each subset. Each application gives one output bit. <bookmark mark='b'/> Noam Nisan and Avi Wigderson showed in 1988 that the small overlaps keep the outputs nearly independent. <bookmark mark='c'/> If some small circuit could tell this output from real coins, a hybrid argument would turn it into a small circuit that computes f, contradicting f's hardness. <bookmark mark='d'/> So the output fools every small circuit, and a randomized algorithm is one. With a logarithmic seed there are only polynomially many seeds: try them all and take the majority. No coins at all.
78c845123259.zh: 第20部分的前沿一章预告过这个想法；下面是它的原理。<bookmark mark='a'/>从一个很短的真随机种子开始，只有对数多位。选出它的许多位置子集，彼此重叠极少，这叫组合设计，再对每个子集施加一个困难函数 f。每施加一次，得到一个输出位。<bookmark mark='b'/>Noam Nisan 和 Avi Wigderson 在1988年证明，重叠很小让这些输出几乎相互独立。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果某个小电路能把这串输出和真硬币区分开，混合论证就能把它变成一个计算 f 的小电路，与 f 的困难性矛盾。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以这串输出骗过每个小电路，而随机算法正是这样的电路。种子是对数长，种子就只有多项式多个：全部试一遍，取多数。完全不用硬币。

050f73820ee9.en: Here is the problem at the centre of derandomization. <bookmark mark='a'/> Is this determinant, the Vandermonde determinant, equal to the product of all the differences? Expanding it for ten variables would produce over three and a half million terms. <bookmark mark='b'/> Instead, pick random values modulo a prime and compare the two sides: about a tenth of a millisecond. Richard DeMillo and Richard Lipton, Jacob Schwartz and Richard Zippel proved that a nonzero polynomial of degree d vanishes at a random point with probability at most d over p. <bookmark mark='c'/> The true identity passed every test. A false one, with a single sign changed, slipped through a little less often than the bound allows when the field is tiny, and never once in five thousand tries over a field of a million. <bookmark mark='d'/> So identity testing has a fast randomized algorithm. Nobody knows a deterministic polynomial one.
050f73820ee9.zh: 这是去随机化的核心问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>这个行列式，范德蒙德行列式，等于所有差的乘积吗？对十个变量把它展开，会产生超过三百五十万项。<bookmark mark='b'/>换个办法：在模一个素数下随机取值，比较两边：大约十分之一毫秒。Richard DeMillo 与 Richard Lipton、Jacob Schwartz 与 Richard Zippel 证明了，一个 d 次的非零多项式在随机点上为零的概率至多是 d 除以 p。<bookmark mark='c'/>真的恒等式通过了每一次测试。一个假的，只改了一个符号，在域很小时蒙混过关的频率略低于界所允许的；在一百万的域上，五千次尝试中一次也没有。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以恒等测试有快速的随机算法。没人知道一个确定性的多项式算法。

af08bebacad2.en: This turns into a striking trade-off. <bookmark mark='a'/> Russell Impagliazzo and Avi Wigderson proved in 1997: if some problem solvable in exponential time requires exponential-size circuits, then P equals BPP. <bookmark mark='b'/> Almost everyone believes that hypothesis, so almost everyone believes randomness gives no extra power to polynomial-time algorithms. <bookmark mark='c'/> The converse holds too, in part: Valentine Kabanets and Impagliazzo showed that removing the coins from polynomial identity testing would itself prove new circuit lower bounds. <bookmark mark='d'/> So derandomization and lower bounds are the same problem seen from two sides. <bookmark mark='e'/> Primality is the poster child: randomized tests since the 1970s, a deterministic polynomial one since 2002. <bookmark mark='f'/> In practice nobody uses the deterministic test: Miller-Rabin is far faster.
af08bebacad2.zh: 这变成了一个惊人的权衡。<bookmark mark='a'/>Russell Impagliazzo 和 Avi Wigderson 在1997年证明：如果某个指数时间可解的问题需要指数规模的电路，那么 P 等于 BPP。<bookmark mark='b'/>几乎所有人都相信这个假设，所以几乎所有人都相信，随机性不给多项式时间算法增加额外的能力。<bookmark mark='c'/>反方向也部分成立：Valentine Kabanets 和 Impagliazzo 证明，从多项式恒等测试中去掉硬币，本身就会证明新的电路下界。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以去随机化和下界是同一个问题的两面。<bookmark mark='e'/>素性判定是招牌例子：从1970年代起就有随机测试，2002年起有了确定性的多项式测试。<bookmark mark='f'/>实践中没人用确定性测试：Miller-Rabin 快得多。

808c63b5e410.en: Circuits give a purely combinatorial way at P versus NP. <bookmark mark='a'/> P slash poly is the class of problems with a polynomial-size circuit for each input length. <bookmark mark='b'/> It contains P, and, by Adleman, BPP. <bookmark mark='c'/> So proving that SAT needs circuits of superpolynomial size would separate P from NP, with no machines involved, only gates. <bookmark mark='d'/> Richard Karp and Richard Lipton showed that if SAT did have small circuits, the polynomial hierarchy would collapse to its second level. <bookmark mark='e'/> So most believe SAT needs large circuits, but proving it runs into Part 26's barriers. <bookmark mark='f'/> What can be proved is lower bounds for restricted circuits. The first success was circuits of constant depth.
808c63b5e410.zh: 电路给出一条纯组合的路，通向 P 与 NP。<bookmark mark='a'/>P/poly 是这样一类问题：每个输入长度都有一个多项式规模的电路。<bookmark mark='b'/>它包含 P，而由 Adleman 定理，也包含 BPP。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以证明 SAT 需要超多项式规模的电路，就能把 P 和 NP 分开，不涉及任何机器，只有门。<bookmark mark='d'/>Richard Karp 和 Richard Lipton 证明，如果 SAT 真有小电路，多项式层级就会塌缩到第二层。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以多数人相信 SAT 需要大电路，但证明它会撞上第26部分的障碍。<bookmark mark='f'/>能证明的是受限电路的下界。第一个成功的是常数深度的电路。

b6b27cb0700e.en: Johan Håstad's tool is the random restriction. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is a formula in disjunctive normal form: twenty terms, each the AND of three literals, OR-ed together, over fourteen variables. <bookmark mark='b'/> Fix each variable to a random value, except that with probability p it stays free. <bookmark mark='c'/> Most terms die: one false literal kills a term. If any term becomes true, the whole formula is true. <bookmark mark='d'/> What survives is tiny. This restriction leaves a function that a decision tree of depth two computes.
b6b27cb0700e.zh: Johan Håstad 的工具是随机限制。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是一个析取范式的公式：二十个项，每项是三个文字的与，再把它们或起来，共十四个变量。<bookmark mark='b'/>把每个变量固定为一个随机值，只是以概率 p 让它保持自由。<bookmark mark='c'/>大多数项死掉了：一个假文字就能杀死一项。只要有一项变真，整个公式就为真。<bookmark mark='d'/>剩下的东西非常小。这个限制留下的函数，用深度为二的决策树就能计算。

58e4d30048f2.en: How often does a restriction leave something complicated? <bookmark mark='a'/> We applied fifteen hundred random restrictions at each value of p and computed the exact decision-tree depth of what was left. Håstad's switching lemma bounds the chance of depth s or more by five p w to the s, and the measured frequencies sit well inside the bound where it applies. <bookmark mark='b'/> A shallow decision tree can be written either way round, so an OR of ANDs switches into an AND of ORs. <bookmark mark='c'/> Apply restrictions repeatedly, and a circuit of constant depth collapses one level at a time. <bookmark mark='d'/> But parity never collapses: restrict it, and you get the parity of the free variables. <bookmark mark='e'/> So parity needs exponentially large circuits of constant depth, the result of Furst, Saxe and Sipser, Ajtai, and Yao, made sharp by Håstad.
58e4d30048f2.zh: 一个限制多久会留下复杂的东西？<bookmark mark='a'/>我们在每个 p 值上施加一千五百个随机限制，并算出剩余函数的精确决策树深度。Håstad 的切换引理把深度达到 s 或以上的概率限制在五 p w 的 s 次方以内，而在这个界适用的地方，测得的频率都远在界内。<bookmark mark='b'/>浅的决策树可以正着写，也可以反着写，所以与的或切换成或的与。<bookmark mark='c'/>反复施加限制，常数深度的电路就一层一层地塌缩。<bookmark mark='d'/>但奇偶函数从不塌缩：限制它，得到的是自由变量的奇偶。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以奇偶函数需要指数大的常数深度电路，这是 Furst、Saxe 与 Sipser，Ajtai，以及 Yao 的结果，由 Håstad 做到了精确。

ebdfca327ec9.en: Other restricted models fell too. <bookmark mark='a'/> Alexander Razborov and Roman Smolensky showed that even with gates counting modulo three, parity needs exponential size; their method approximates the whole circuit by a polynomial of low degree. Razborov also proved that monotone circuits, with no negations, need superpolynomial size for clique. And Ryan Williams separated nondeterministic exponential time from ACC zero. <bookmark mark='b'/> His proof is unusual: a satisfiability algorithm for those circuits, only slightly faster than trying all two to the n inputs, implies a lower bound against them. <bookmark mark='c'/> Algorithms imply lower bounds. It is the one method so far that has crossed the barriers of Part 26.
ebdfca327ec9.zh: 其他受限模型也相继被攻破。<bookmark mark='a'/>Alexander Razborov 和 Roman Smolensky 证明，即使允许模三计数的门，奇偶函数仍需要指数规模；他们的方法是用一个低次多项式近似整个电路。Razborov 还证明，没有非门的单调电路计算团问题需要超多项式规模。而 Ryan Williams 把非确定指数时间和 ACC 零分开了。<bookmark mark='b'/>他的证明很不寻常：对这类电路，一个只比尝试全部二的 n 次方个输入稍快一点的可满足性算法，就意味着对它们的下界。<bookmark mark='c'/>算法蕴含下界。这是迄今唯一越过了第26部分那些障碍的方法。

ca3cab3b08c0.en: In 1979 Andrew Yao asked a clean question: if Alice holds one input and Bob another, how many bits must they exchange to compute something about both? <bookmark mark='a'/> Take equality. Are two n-bit strings the same? <bookmark mark='b'/> With randomness it is cheap. Alice treats her string as a polynomial, picks a random point, and sends the point and the value: Part 20's fingerprint as a protocol. Different strings agree at a random point with probability at most n over q. <bookmark mark='c'/> On strings of a thousand bits differing in a single place, with a field of a million, our twenty thousand trials never erred. For strings of a trillion bits, a hundred and sixty-two bits are enough. <bookmark mark='d'/> Without randomness, Alice must send all n bits, and that can be proved.
ca3cab3b08c0.zh: 1979年，姚期智提出了一个干净的问题：如果 Alice 持有一个输入，Bob 持有另一个，要计算关于两者的某个量，他们必须交换多少位？<bookmark mark='a'/>以相等为例。两个 n 位串相同吗？<bookmark mark='b'/>有了随机性，这很便宜。Alice 把她的串看作一个多项式，随机取一个点，把这个点和取值发过去：第20部分的指纹，做成了协议。不同的串在随机点上相等的概率至多是 n 除以 q。<bookmark mark='c'/>对只有一处不同的一千位串，在一百万的域上，我们两万次试验从未出错。对一万亿位的串，一百六十二位就够了。<bookmark mark='d'/>没有随机性，Alice 必须发送全部 n 位，而这可以证明。

b60cfbe61d3f.en: How do you prove that a protocol needs many bits? <bookmark mark='a'/> Write the function as a matrix, Alice's input for the row, Bob's for the column. A protocol that exchanges c bits cuts this matrix into at most two to the c rectangles, each constant. <bookmark mark='b'/> For equality the matrix is the identity. No rectangle can contain two diagonal ones, because a rectangle containing x, x and y, y also contains x, y, which is zero. <bookmark mark='c'/> So two to the n rectangles are needed, and n bits. <bookmark mark='d'/> Linear algebra gives the same bound through the rank of the matrix. <bookmark mark='e'/> Some functions resist even randomness. Deciding whether two sets intersect needs a linear number of bits, randomized or not. <bookmark mark='f'/> And whether the logarithm of the rank always predicts the true cost, up to a polynomial, is the log-rank conjecture, open since 1988.
b60cfbe61d3f.zh: 怎样证明一个协议需要很多位？<bookmark mark='a'/>把函数写成矩阵，Alice 的输入作行，Bob 的作列。一个交换 c 位的协议把这个矩阵切成至多二的 c 次方个矩形，每个矩形取值不变。<bookmark mark='b'/>对相等问题，矩阵是单位阵。没有哪个矩形能包含两个对角线上的一：包含 x, x 和 y, y 的矩形也包含 x, y，而那里是零。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以需要二的 n 次方个矩形，也就是 n 位。<bookmark mark='d'/>线性代数通过矩阵的秩给出同样的界。<bookmark mark='e'/>有些函数连随机性也对付不了。判定两个集合是否相交需要线性多位，不论随机与否。<bookmark mark='f'/>而秩的对数是否总能在多项式意义上预测真实代价，就是对数秩猜想，自1988年起悬而未决。

f560976fe13a.en: This explains a design choice from Part 20. <bookmark mark='a'/> A streaming algorithm with s bits of memory is a one-way protocol: Alice runs it on the first half of the stream and hands its memory to Bob. <bookmark mark='b'/> So any stream question that would answer disjointness needs linear memory. <bookmark mark='c'/> Exact distinct counts, exact frequency moments and the exact most frequent item all fall this way. <bookmark mark='d'/> Noga Alon, Yossi Matias and Mario Szegedy proved these bounds in 1996, alongside the sketches. <bookmark mark='e'/> HyperLogLog and Count-Min approximate because they must.
f560976fe13a.zh: 这解释了第20部分的一个设计选择。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个有 s 位内存的流式算法就是一个单向协议：Alice 在数据流的前一半上运行它，再把内存交给 Bob。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以任何能回答不相交问题的流式问题，都需要线性内存。<bookmark mark='c'/>精确的不同元素计数、精确的频率矩、精确的最频繁元素，都这样倒下了。<bookmark mark='d'/>Noga Alon、Yossi Matias 和 Mario Szegedy 在1996年与那些草图算法一起证明了这些界。<bookmark mark='e'/>HyperLogLog 和 Count-Min 做近似，是因为它们不得不如此。

7a041fef48c0.en: How do you prove that two graphs are different? For sameness, the matching of vertices is a short certificate. For difference, none is known. But a conversation works. <bookmark mark='a'/> The verifier flips a coin, picks one of the two graphs, scrambles its vertex labels, and shows the result to the prover. <bookmark mark='b'/> The prover, who has unlimited computing power, says which graph it came from. <bookmark mark='c'/> The verifier accepts if the answer matches the coin. <bookmark mark='d'/> If the graphs really differ, the prover can always tell, and our honest prover was right every time. <bookmark mark='e'/> If they are the same, the scrambled graph carries no information about the coin, and the prover can only guess: forty-nine percent in our two thousand rounds. <bookmark mark='f'/> Twenty rounds push a bluffer's chances below one in a million. <bookmark mark='g'/> Interaction has proved something no known written proof can.
7a041fef48c0.zh: 怎样证明两个图是不同的？要证明相同，顶点的对应关系就是一份简短的证书。要证明不同，还不知道有什么证书。但一场对话可以做到。<bookmark mark='a'/>验证者抛一枚硬币，选出两个图之一，打乱它的顶点标号，把结果给证明者看。<bookmark mark='b'/>拥有无限计算能力的证明者说出它来自哪个图。<bookmark mark='c'/>答案与硬币一致，验证者就接受。<bookmark mark='d'/>如果两个图真的不同，证明者总能分辨，我们诚实的证明者每次都答对了。<bookmark mark='e'/>如果它们相同，打乱后的图不带有关于硬币的任何信息，证明者只能猜：在我们的两千轮里是百分之四十九。<bookmark mark='f'/>二十轮就能把虚张声势者的机会压到百万分之一以下。<bookmark mark='g'/>交互证明了一件已知的书面证明都证明不了的事。

7906a3f4de44.en: The general setting is called IP. <bookmark mark='a'/> A verifier that runs in polynomial time and flips coins exchanges messages with an all-powerful prover. <bookmark mark='b'/> True statements must be accepted with high probability, <bookmark mark='c'/> and false ones rejected with high probability, whatever the prover tries. <bookmark mark='d'/> Shafi Goldwasser, Silvio Micali and Charles Rackoff introduced the idea in 1985, together with the question of how much knowledge a proof conveys. <bookmark mark='e'/> László Babai independently defined Arthur-Merlin games, in which the verifier's coins are shown to the prover. <bookmark mark='f'/> Goldwasser and Sipser showed that hiding the coins makes no difference. <bookmark mark='g'/> NP is the special case with one message and no coins. How much more does interaction give? The answer is the next chapter.
7906a3f4de44.zh: 一般的框架叫作 IP。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个多项式时间、会抛硬币的验证者，与一个全能的证明者交换消息。<bookmark mark='b'/>真命题必须以高概率被接受，<bookmark mark='c'/>假命题必须以高概率被拒绝，不论证明者怎样尝试。<bookmark mark='d'/>Shafi Goldwasser、Silvio Micali 和 Charles Rackoff 在1985年提出了这个想法，同时提出了一个证明传递多少知识的问题。<bookmark mark='e'/>László Babai 独立地定义了 Arthur-Merlin 博弈，其中验证者的硬币对证明者公开。<bookmark mark='f'/>Goldwasser 和 Sipser 证明，藏起硬币没有区别。<bookmark mark='g'/>NP 是只有一条消息、没有硬币的特例。交互还能多给多少？答案在下一章。

3e76321339af.en: Chapter six. Sum-check and IP equals PSPACE.
3e76321339af.zh: 第6章。Sum-check 与 IP 等于 PSPACE。

d52888fa964b.en: In 1990 Carsten Lund, Lance Fortnow, Howard Karloff and Noam Nisan found the key idea: turn logic into algebra. <bookmark mark='a'/> Not x becomes one minus x; and becomes multiplication; an OR of three literals becomes one minus the product of their negations. <bookmark mark='b'/> On zeros and ones this polynomial agrees with the formula, so the number of satisfying assignments is the sum of the polynomial over the Boolean cube. <bookmark mark='c'/> But the polynomial is also defined at any point of a finite field; we use the integers modulo ninety-seven. Its degree in each variable is at most the number of clauses, five. <bookmark mark='d'/> The prover claims the sum is seven. <bookmark mark='e'/> The verifier cannot add up two to the n terms. Here is how it checks anyway.
d52888fa964b.zh: 1990年，Carsten Lund、Lance Fortnow、Howard Karloff 和 Noam Nisan 找到了关键想法：把逻辑变成代数。<bookmark mark='a'/>非 x 变成一减 x；与变成乘法；三个文字的或，变成一减去它们否定的乘积。<bookmark mark='b'/>在零和一上，这个多项式与公式一致，所以满足赋值的个数，就是这个多项式在布尔立方体上的和。<bookmark mark='c'/>但这个多项式在有限域的任何点上也有定义；我们用模九十七的整数。它在每个变量上的次数至多是子句数，五。<bookmark mark='d'/>证明者声称这个和是七。<bookmark mark='e'/>验证者没法把二的 n 次方项加起来。下面看它怎样照样检查。

60992c184d72.en: The protocol peels off one variable per round. <bookmark mark='a'/> In round one the prover sends a polynomial in a single variable: the sum with x one left free and everything else summed over zero and one. It sends it as six values, enough to pin down a polynomial of degree five. <bookmark mark='b'/> The verifier checks that its values at zero and one add up to the claim, seven, then picks a random field element, thirty, and the claim becomes the polynomial's value there: thirty-three. Round two does the same with x one fixed at thirty, and so on. <bookmark mark='c'/> After the last round the verifier evaluates the arithmetized formula once, at the four random values, and gets ninety-one, exactly the final claim. Accept. <bookmark mark='d'/> The verifier did a few field operations per round and a single evaluation, instead of adding up two to the n terms.
60992c184d72.zh: 协议每轮剥掉一个变量。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一轮，证明者发来一个单变量多项式：让 x 一保持自由，其余变量都对零和一求和。它以六个值的形式发送，足以确定一个五次多项式。<bookmark mark='b'/>验证者检查它在零和一处的值之和等于声称值七，然后随机取一个域元素，三十，声称值就变成多项式在那里的值：三十三。第二轮把 x 一固定为三十，做同样的事，依此类推。<bookmark mark='c'/>最后一轮之后，验证者在四个随机值处把算术化的公式求值一次，得到九十一，恰好等于最后的声称值。接受。<bookmark mark='d'/>验证者每轮只做几次域运算，再加一次求值，而不是把二的 n 次方项加起来。

f5da34dbca5a.en: What if the prover lies? <bookmark mark='a'/> Say it claims eight. Its first polynomial must add up to eight at zero and one, so it is not the true polynomial. <bookmark mark='b'/> Two different polynomials of degree d agree on at most d points. <bookmark mark='c'/> So the only hope is that the verifier's random point happens to be one where the false polynomial and the true one agree; then the lie disappears. That happens with probability at most d over p. <bookmark mark='d'/> Otherwise the false claim moves into the next round, and if it survives every round, the final evaluation exposes it. <bookmark mark='e'/> We built the best possible cheater, one whose false polynomial agrees with the true one at as many points as it can. Modulo ninety-seven, it survived nineteen point three percent of three thousand runs, against a bound of nineteen point one. <bookmark mark='f'/> With a field of a million elements, it never survived.
f5da34dbca5a.zh: 如果证明者撒谎呢？<bookmark mark='a'/>比如它声称是八。它的第一个多项式在零和一处之和必须是八，所以它不是真正的多项式。<bookmark mark='b'/>两个不同的 d 次多项式至多在 d 个点上相等。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以唯一的希望是，验证者的随机点恰好落在假多项式与真多项式相等的地方；这时谎言就消失了。这种事发生的概率至多是 d 除以 p。<bookmark mark='d'/>否则，假的声称就带进下一轮；如果它撑过了每一轮，最后的求值会揭穿它。<bookmark mark='e'/>我们造了最好的作弊者，它的假多项式与真多项式在尽可能多的点上相等。模九十七时，它在三千次运行中存活了百分之十九点三，而界是十九点一。<bookmark mark='f'/>在一百万元素的域上，它一次也没存活。

6a077f015918.en: This was a breakthrough. <bookmark mark='a'/> Sum-check shows that counting solutions has interactive proofs, far beyond NP. <bookmark mark='b'/> Weeks later Adi Shamir extended it to quantified formulas: a for-all becomes a product, an exists becomes one minus a product, and the same round-by-round checking works. <bookmark mark='c'/> A trick to keep the degree low makes it go through n quantifiers. <bookmark mark='d'/> In the other direction, an optimal prover can be simulated in polynomial space. <bookmark mark='e'/> So IP equals PSPACE: a polynomial-time verifier with coins can be convinced of anything provable in polynomial space, such as who wins a board game from a given position. <bookmark mark='f'/> And the proof does not relativize: there are oracles relative to which it is false. It was the first major technique to get past Part 26's first barrier.
6a077f015918.zh: 这是一个突破。<bookmark mark='a'/>Sum-check 表明，计数解的个数也有交互式证明，远远超出 NP。<bookmark mark='b'/>几周后，Adi Shamir 把它推广到量化公式：全称变成乘积，存在变成一减乘积，同样逐轮检查的办法依然管用。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个保持次数很低的技巧让它能通过 n 个量词。<bookmark mark='d'/>反方向上，最优的证明者可以在多项式空间里模拟。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以 IP 等于 PSPACE：一个带硬币的多项式时间验证者，可以被说服相信任何能在多项式空间里证明的事，比如从给定局面出发谁能赢一盘棋。<bookmark mark='f'/>而且这个证明不可相对化：存在预言机，相对于它这个结论不成立。它是第一个越过第26部分第一道障碍的重大技术。

76f376985101.en: Here is the classic story. <bookmark mark='a'/> A cave is shaped like a ring, with a door at the back that opens only with a secret word. <bookmark mark='b'/> Peggy walks in by one of two paths while Victor waits outside. Then Victor shouts which path she should come back by. <bookmark mark='c'/> If she knows the word, she can always comply, opening the door if needed. If not, she is caught half the time. <bookmark mark='d'/> After twenty rounds, a bluffer survives with probability one in a million. <bookmark mark='e'/> And Victor learns nothing about the word. He could have produced an identical video with an actor who doesn't know it, by simply editing out the failed rounds. <bookmark mark='f'/> That is the definition of zero knowledge: whatever the verifier sees, he could have simulated himself.
76f376985101.zh: 这是一个经典故事。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个山洞呈环形，后面有一扇门，只有念出秘密口令才能打开。<bookmark mark='b'/>Peggy 从两条路之一走进去，Victor 在外面等着。然后 Victor 喊出她应该从哪条路回来。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果她知道口令，总能照办，必要时打开那扇门。如果不知道，她有一半的时候会被抓住。<bookmark mark='d'/>二十轮之后，虚张声势者存活的概率是百万分之一。<bookmark mark='e'/>而 Victor 对口令一无所知。他本可以找一个不知道口令的演员拍出一模一样的视频，只要把失败的回合剪掉。<bookmark mark='f'/>这就是零知识的定义：验证者看到的一切，他都能自己模拟出来。

a297a5092675.en: Oded Goldreich, Silvio Micali and Avi Wigderson showed in 1986 that every problem in NP has a zero-knowledge proof, through three-colouring. Here is the Petersen graph, which the prover knows how to colour. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each round, the prover first shuffles the three colours at random, <bookmark mark='b'/> then commits to every vertex's colour, here by publishing a hash of a random nonce and the colour. It cannot change a colour later, and the hash reveals nothing. <bookmark mark='c'/> The verifier points at one edge. <bookmark mark='d'/> The prover opens the two commitments at its ends, <bookmark mark='e'/> and the verifier checks that the colours differ and the hashes match. Then everything starts again with a fresh shuffle.
a297a5092675.zh: Oded Goldreich、Silvio Micali 和 Avi Wigderson 在1986年证明，通过三着色，NP 中的每个问题都有零知识证明。这是 Petersen 图，证明者知道怎样给它着色。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一轮，证明者先随机打乱三种颜色，<bookmark mark='b'/>然后对每个顶点的颜色做承诺，这里是公布一个随机数和颜色拼起来的哈希。之后它不能再改颜色，而哈希不泄露任何信息。<bookmark mark='c'/>验证者指定一条边。<bookmark mark='d'/>证明者打开边两端的两个承诺，<bookmark mark='e'/>验证者检查两种颜色不同、哈希吻合。然后一切重新开始，换一次新的打乱。

a08464f65c6e.en: Is it sound? <bookmark mark='a'/> We gave a cheating prover a colouring with two bad edges out of fifteen. <bookmark mark='b'/> It is caught whenever the verifier picks one of them. <bookmark mark='c'/> In two thousand runs, the fraction still undetected after k rounds follows one minus two fifteenths to the k: forty-seven percent after five rounds, six percent after twenty. A cheater with a single bad edge survives longer, one minus one over m to the k. <bookmark mark='d'/> Three hundred and one rounds push even that below one in a billion.
a08464f65c6e.zh: 它可靠吗？<bookmark mark='a'/>我们给一个作弊的证明者一种着色，十五条边中有两条是坏的。<bookmark mark='b'/>只要验证者选中其中之一，它就被抓住。<bookmark mark='c'/>在两千次运行中，k 轮后仍未被发现的比例服从一减十五分之二的 k 次方：五轮后百分之四十七，二十轮后百分之六。只有一条坏边的作弊者撑得更久，是一减 m 分之一的 k 次方。<bookmark mark='d'/>三百零一轮能把它也压到十亿分之一以下。

46caa49ef129.en: And what does the verifier learn? <bookmark mark='a'/> In each round it sees two different colours at the ends of an edge. Because the colours were freshly shuffled, the pair is uniformly random. <bookmark mark='b'/> A simulator that knows no colouring at all can produce exactly the same thing: pick two different colours at random. <bookmark mark='c'/> Over six thousand rounds each, the real and simulated transcripts show every ordered pair about one sixth of the time. <bookmark mark='d'/> Anything the verifier could compute from the conversation, it could have computed from the simulation, so it learns nothing beyond the fact that the graph is colourable. <bookmark mark='e'/> Amos Fiat and Adi Shamir showed how to replace the verifier's coins with a hash of the conversation, turning such proofs into signatures; Part 30 uses it, and so do today's blockchains.
46caa49ef129.zh: 那验证者学到了什么？<bookmark mark='a'/>每一轮，它看到一条边两端的两种不同颜色。因为颜色是刚刚打乱的，这一对颜色是均匀随机的。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个根本不知道任何着色的模拟器，可以产生完全相同的东西：随机挑两种不同的颜色。<bookmark mark='c'/>各六千轮下来，真实记录和模拟记录中，每一种有序颜色对出现的频率都约为六分之一。<bookmark mark='d'/>验证者能从对话中算出的任何东西，它都能从模拟中算出，所以除了这个图可以着色之外，它什么也没学到。<bookmark mark='e'/>Amos Fiat 和 Adi Shamir 展示了怎样用对话的哈希代替验证者的硬币，把这类证明变成签名；第30部分会用到它，今天的区块链也在用。

4f021e1502ca.en: Here is the most surprising theorem in this part. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take any statement with an NP proof, say that a formula is satisfiable. The proof can be rewritten, in polynomial length, in a special robust format, so that a verifier who flips a logarithmic number of coins and reads just a constant number of bits of it can check it. <bookmark mark='b'/> A correct proof is always accepted. <bookmark mark='c'/> If the statement is false, every purported proof is rejected at least half the time. <bookmark mark='d'/> That is the PCP theorem, proved in 1992 by Sanjeev Arora and Shmuel Safra, and Arora, Carsten Lund, Rajeev Motwani, Madhu Sudan and Mario Szegedy. <bookmark mark='e'/> Johan Håstad later showed that three bits suffice. Reading three bits of a proof, chosen at random, is as convincing as reading all of it, given a proof written the right way.
4f021e1502ca.zh: 这是这一部分最令人惊讶的定理。<bookmark mark='a'/>任取一个有 NP 证明的命题，比如某个公式可满足。这个证明可以用多项式长度、以一种特殊的稳健格式重写，使得一个只抛对数多枚硬币、只读其中常数多位的验证者就能检查它。<bookmark mark='b'/>正确的证明总被接受。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果命题是假的，每一份声称的证明至少有一半的时候被拒绝。<bookmark mark='d'/>这就是 PCP 定理，1992年由 Sanjeev Arora 与 Shmuel Safra，以及 Arora、Carsten Lund、Rajeev Motwani、Madhu Sudan 与 Mario Szegedy 证明。<bookmark mark='e'/>Johan Håstad 后来证明三位就够了。只要证明写得得法，随机读它的三位，就和读完全部一样令人信服。

f674d4cabdf2.en: The full proof is long, but its flavour fits in a small experiment. <bookmark mark='a'/> Is a Boolean function on eight bits a parity, the exclusive or of some subset of its inputs? <bookmark mark='b'/> Manuel Blum, Michael Luby and Ronitt Rubinfeld proposed a test: pick two random inputs x and y, and check that f of x plus f of y equals f of x exclusive-or y. <bookmark mark='c'/> It reads three values, and parities always pass. <bookmark mark='d'/> We took a parity, corrupted it in more and more places, and computed the exact probability that the test rejects. <bookmark mark='e'/> For small distances it follows three delta minus six delta squared, the bound proved by Mihir Bellare and coauthors. <bookmark mark='f'/> A function far from every parity is caught often. PCP constructions encode proofs so that every wrong proof is far from every right one, and tests like this one find the difference.
f674d4cabdf2.zh: 完整的证明很长，但它的味道可以装进一个小实验。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个八位输入的布尔函数是不是奇偶函数，即某个输入子集的异或？<bookmark mark='b'/>Manuel Blum、Michael Luby 和 Ronitt Rubinfeld 提出了一个测试：随机取两个输入 x 和 y，检查 f(x) 加 f(y) 是否等于 f(x 异或 y)。<bookmark mark='c'/>它读三个值，奇偶函数总能通过。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们拿一个奇偶函数，在越来越多的地方把它改坏，并算出测试拒绝的精确概率。<bookmark mark='e'/>距离小的时候，它服从三 delta 减六 delta 平方，这是 Mihir Bellare 等人证明的界。<bookmark mark='f'/>离每个奇偶函数都很远的函数经常被抓住。PCP 的构造这样编码证明：每个错误的证明都离每个正确的证明很远，而像这样的测试能发现差别。

4e1b2f5454ea.en: In 2005 Irit Dinur gave a new proof, combinatorial and much shorter. <bookmark mark='a'/> Think of a proof as an assignment to a graph of constraints. <bookmark mark='b'/> Satisfiability already gives a graph where, if the formula is unsatisfiable, at least one constraint fails: a gap of one constraint. <bookmark mark='c'/> Each step of Dinur's proof turns the graph into an expander, the kind Part 56 studies, and replaces constraints by walks on it, doubling the fraction of violated constraints. <bookmark mark='d'/> A second step shrinks the alphabet back down, losing only a constant factor. <bookmark mark='e'/> After logarithmically many rounds, a constant fraction of constraints must fail, and the graph is still polynomial: that is the PCP theorem. <bookmark mark='f'/> A result first proved with heavy algebra became a forty-page combinatorial argument.
4e1b2f5454ea.zh: 2005年，Irit Dinur 给出了一个新证明，是组合的，而且短得多。<bookmark mark='a'/>把证明看作一个约束图上的赋值。<bookmark mark='b'/>可满足性本身就给出这样一个图：若公式不可满足，至少一个约束失败：一个约束的间隙。<bookmark mark='c'/>Dinur 证明的每一步把图变成扩展图，也就是第56部分研究的那种，并用图上的游走代替约束，使违反约束的比例翻倍。<bookmark mark='d'/>第二步再把字母表缩回来，只损失一个常数因子。<bookmark mark='e'/>经过对数多轮之后，必须有常数比例的约束失败，而图仍是多项式大小：这就是 PCP 定理。<bookmark mark='f'/>一个最初靠繁重代数证明的结果，变成了四十页的组合论证。

1d3e358feb6c.en: Why does a statement about proofs matter for algorithms? <bookmark mark='a'/> Read each of the verifier's possible tests as a constraint on the proof bits, so a proof is an assignment. <bookmark mark='b'/> If the statement is true, some assignment satisfies every constraint. <bookmark mark='c'/> If it is false, every assignment violates a constant fraction. <bookmark mark='d'/> So an algorithm that could tell these two cases apart, or approximate the best fraction within that gap, would decide SAT. Feige, Goldwasser, Lovász, Safra and Szegedy found this connection in 1991, before the theorem itself.
1d3e358feb6c.zh: 一个关于证明的命题，为什么对算法重要？<bookmark mark='a'/>把验证者每一种可能的测试读作对证明各位的一条约束，于是证明就是一个赋值。<bookmark mark='b'/>若命题为真，某个赋值满足每条约束。<bookmark mark='c'/>若命题为假，每个赋值都违反常数比例的约束。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以一个能分辨这两种情形、或者在这个间隙之内近似最优比例的算法，就能判定 SAT。Feige、Goldwasser、Lovász、Safra 和 Szegedy 在1991年发现了这个联系，早于定理本身。

fd52466da7a9.en: The sharpest example is MAX-3SAT: satisfy as many three-literal clauses as possible. <bookmark mark='a'/> Flip a coin for every variable. Each clause fails only if all three literals do, with probability one eighth, so a random assignment satisfies seven eighths of the clauses on average. Our measurements: eighty-seven and a half percent, every time. <bookmark mark='b'/> Johan Håstad proved in 2001 that doing even slightly better than seven eighths, on formulas that are fully satisfiable, is NP-hard. <bookmark mark='c'/> The coin is optimal. <bookmark mark='d'/> On random formulas, of course, local search finds assignments satisfying ninety-seven to a hundred percent. Hardness of approximation is about the worst case.
fd52466da7a9.zh: 最鲜明的例子是 MAX-3SAT：满足尽可能多的三文字子句。<bookmark mark='a'/>给每个变量抛一枚硬币。每个子句只有三个文字都失败时才失败，概率八分之一，所以随机赋值平均满足八分之七的子句。我们的测量：每次都是百分之八十七点五。<bookmark mark='b'/>Johan Håstad 在2001年证明，在完全可满足的公式上，哪怕比八分之七好一点点也是 NP 难的。<bookmark mark='c'/>硬币是最优的。<bookmark mark='d'/>当然，在随机公式上，局部搜索能找到满足百分之九十七到一百的赋值。近似的困难性说的是最坏情况。

36f1b3baecc3.en: For several problems the PCP theorem gives exactly matching limits. <bookmark mark='a'/> MAX-3SAT, at seven eighths. Linear equations modulo two, at a half: a random assignment again. Set cover, where the greedy algorithm's factor of ln n cannot be improved. Clique, which cannot be approximated within n to the one minus epsilon. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then vertex cover, where the simple algorithm of Part 23 gets within a factor two but hardness is only known below the square root of two, and MAX-CUT, where Goemans and Williamson's semidefinite programming gets point eight seven eight and hardness stops at sixteen seventeenths. <bookmark mark='c'/> Those gaps are the subject of the next chapter.
36f1b3baecc3.zh: 对好几个问题，PCP 定理给出恰好吻合的极限。<bookmark mark='a'/>MAX-3SAT，在八分之七。模二线性方程组，在二分之一：又是随机赋值。集合覆盖，贪心算法的 ln n 因子无法改进。团，无法在 n 的一减 epsilon 次方之内近似。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后是顶点覆盖，第23部分的简单算法能做到两倍以内，但已知的困难性只到根号二以下；还有最大割，Goemans 和 Williamson 的半定规划能做到零点八七八，而困难性止于十七分之十六。<bookmark mark='c'/>这些间隙就是下一章的主题。

ea5c5f16cfe5.en: Chapter ten. The Unique Games Conjecture.

3e400b6d6d3d.en: In 2002 Subhash Khot proposed a conjecture about a simple kind of constraint problem. <bookmark mark='a'/> Give each vertex a label from zero to k minus one. Each edge demands that the label at one end equal the label at the other plus some constant, modulo k. A label on one end determines the other uniquely: hence unique games. <bookmark mark='b'/> If every constraint can be met, there is an easy algorithm: fix one label and propagate. <bookmark mark='c'/> Khot conjectured that telling apart games where nearly all constraints can be met from games where almost none can is NP-hard. <bookmark mark='d'/> Nearly satisfiable is exactly where propagation fails: a single violated edge sends the labels astray.
3e400b6d6d3d.zh: 2002年，Subhash Khot 就一类简单的约束问题提出了一个猜想。<bookmark mark='a'/>给每个顶点一个从零到 k 减一的标签。每条边要求一端的标签等于另一端的标签加上某个常数，模 k。一端的标签唯一决定另一端：所以叫唯一博弈。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果每条约束都能满足，有一个简单的算法：固定一个标签，然后传播。<bookmark mark='c'/>Khot 猜想，把几乎所有约束都能满足的博弈，与几乎没有约束能满足的博弈区分开，是 NP 难的。<bookmark mark='d'/>几乎可满足，恰恰是传播失效的地方：一条被违反的边就会把标签带偏。

5afca76cb837.en: We can watch propagation fail. We planted a labelling on three thousand vertices and nine thousand edges, with seven labels, then corrupted a fraction epsilon of the constraints. <bookmark mark='a'/> With no corruption, propagation from any vertex satisfies every constraint. <bookmark mark='b'/> With five percent corrupted, the hidden labelling still satisfies ninety-five percent, but propagation gets only eighty-three: each bad edge in the search tree corrupts everything below it. <bookmark mark='c'/> At twenty percent, propagation falls to a half, and random labels get one seventh. <bookmark mark='d'/> A semidefinite program does much better, losing only about the square root of epsilon log k, as Moses Charikar and Konstantin and Yury Makarychev showed in 2006. <bookmark mark='e'/> The conjecture says that, up to constants, nothing efficient can do better.
5afca76cb837.zh: 我们可以看着传播失败。我们在三千个顶点、九千条边上埋下一种标签，用七种标签，然后改坏比例为 epsilon 的约束。<bookmark mark='a'/>没有改坏时，从任何顶点传播都满足每条约束。<bookmark mark='b'/>改坏百分之五时，埋下的标签仍满足百分之九十五，但传播只得到八十三：搜索树里每条坏边，都会把它下面的一切带坏。<bookmark mark='c'/>到百分之二十，传播跌到一半，而随机标签得到七分之一。<bookmark mark='d'/>半定规划好得多，只损失大约 epsilon 乘 log k 的平方根，这是 Moses Charikar 与 Konstantin、Yury Makarychev 兄弟在2006年证明的。<bookmark mark='e'/>猜想说，在常数意义上，没有任何高效算法能做得更好。

890a27fa9cd9.en: Part 23 met the conjecture's consequences; here is the whole picture. <bookmark mark='a'/> If it holds, the factor two for vertex cover is optimal, <bookmark mark='b'/> and so is Goemans and Williamson's point eight seven eight for MAX-CUT. <bookmark mark='c'/> Prasad Raghavendra showed in 2008 that it would make one semidefinite program the optimal approximation algorithm for every constraint satisfaction problem at once. <bookmark mark='d'/> There is evidence against it: Sanjeev Arora, Boaz Barak and David Steurer found an algorithm for unique games that is subexponential. <bookmark mark='e'/> And evidence for it: in 2018 Subhash Khot, Dor Minzer and Muli Safra proved the 2-to-2 theorem, a slightly weaker version, <bookmark mark='f'/> which already shows vertex cover is hard to approximate below the square root of two. <bookmark mark='g'/> The conjecture itself remains open.
890a27fa9cd9.zh: 第23部分见过这个猜想的推论；下面是全貌。<bookmark mark='a'/>如果它成立，顶点覆盖的两倍因子就是最优的，<bookmark mark='b'/>Goemans 和 Williamson 在最大割上的零点八七八也是。<bookmark mark='c'/>Prasad Raghavendra 在2008年证明，它会让同一个半定规划，一举成为每个约束满足问题的最优近似算法。<bookmark mark='d'/>也有反对它的证据：Sanjeev Arora、Boaz Barak 和 David Steurer 找到了唯一博弈的亚指数算法。<bookmark mark='e'/>还有支持它的证据：2018年，Subhash Khot、Dor Minzer 和 Muli Safra 证明了二对二定理，一个稍弱的版本，<bookmark mark='f'/>它已经表明顶点覆盖难以近似到根号二以下。<bookmark mark='g'/>猜想本身仍未解决。

2ed71ac494c1.en: NP-hardness separates polynomial from exponential. Many practical questions are finer: is quadratic time really necessary? <bookmark mark='a'/> Fine-grained complexity answers with a few conjectures. The strong exponential time hypothesis says satisfiability with long clauses cannot be solved much faster than two to the n. Part 21 used it for edit distance. The 3SUM conjecture, that finding three numbers summing to zero needs quadratic time, explains why many geometry problems from Part 22 resist faster algorithms. And the all-pairs shortest paths conjecture covers a family of cubic graph problems. <bookmark mark='b'/> The link from SAT to quadratic problems is a beautiful trick of Ryan Williams. Split the variables into two halves, and turn each half-assignment into a vector with one coordinate per clause, zero if that half already satisfies the clause. <bookmark mark='c'/> Two vectors are orthogonal exactly when together they satisfy every clause. <bookmark mark='d'/> So a truly subquadratic algorithm for orthogonal vectors would break the strong exponential time hypothesis. <bookmark mark='e'/> These questions are not about P versus NP. They are about exponents.
2ed71ac494c1.zh: NP 难把多项式和指数分开。许多实际问题更精细：平方时间真的必要吗？<bookmark mark='a'/>细粒度复杂性用几个猜想来回答。强指数时间假设说，长子句的可满足性不可能比二的 n 次方快很多。第21部分用它处理了编辑距离。3SUM 猜想说，找出和为零的三个数需要平方时间，它解释了为什么第22部分的许多几何问题抗拒更快的算法。而全源最短路径猜想覆盖了一族立方时间的图问题。<bookmark mark='b'/>从 SAT 到平方时间问题的联系，是 Ryan Williams 的一个漂亮技巧。把变量分成两半，把每个半赋值变成一个向量，每个子句一个坐标，如果这一半已经满足该子句，这个坐标就是零。<bookmark mark='c'/>两个向量正交，当且仅当它们合起来满足每个子句。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以正交向量问题若有真正低于平方的算法，就会打破强指数时间假设。<bookmark mark='e'/>这些问题不是关于 P 与 NP 的。它们关心的是指数。

df18a16d794c.en: We ran the reduction. <bookmark mark='a'/> Six random formulas, each with twenty-four variables and a hundred and one clauses. Each half of the variables gives four thousand and ninety-six vectors, one coordinate per clause. <bookmark mark='b'/> On every formula, searching for an orthogonal pair gives the same answer as our SAT solver. <bookmark mark='c'/> And the number of pairs is four thousand and ninety-six squared, which is two to the twenty-four: exactly the number of assignments. Brute-force orthogonal vectors is brute-force SAT. <bookmark mark='d'/> So any algorithm that beats N squared by a polynomial factor would beat two to the n for satisfiability. The slow rows are the unsatisfiable formulas, where every pair has to be checked.
df18a16d794c.zh: 我们运行了这个归约。<bookmark mark='a'/>六个随机公式，每个有二十四个变量、一百零一个子句。每一半变量给出四千零九十六个向量，每个子句一个坐标。<bookmark mark='b'/>在每个公式上，寻找正交对给出的答案都与我们的 SAT 求解器一致。<bookmark mark='c'/>而向量对的个数是四千零九十六的平方，等于二的二十四次方：恰好是赋值的个数。暴力求解正交向量，就是暴力求解 SAT。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以任何把 N 平方改进一个多项式因子的算法，都会在可满足性上胜过二的 n 次方。慢的那几行是不可满足的公式，那里每一对都得检查。

7141846b7bb5.en: Here are the two baselines on this machine. <bookmark mark='a'/> We fed both algorithms instances with no solution, so they had to do all their work. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each doubling of n costs about four times as much: quadratic. Four thousand vectors take six tenths of a second; four thousand numbers, three quarters. <bookmark mark='c'/> The conjectures are delicate: Allan Grønlund and Seth Pettie shaved logarithmic factors off 3SUM in 2014, so the conjecture now asks only that no polynomial improvement exists. <bookmark mark='d'/> For an engineer, a conditional lower bound is a stopping rule: stop looking for a better exponent, and work on constants, parallelism or approximation instead.
7141846b7bb5.zh: 这是两个基准算法在这台机器上的表现。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们给两个算法喂的都是无解的实例，所以它们必须做完全部工作。<bookmark mark='b'/>n 每翻一倍，代价约为四倍：平方。四千个向量要十分之六秒；四千个数，四分之三秒。<bookmark mark='c'/>这些猜想很微妙：Allan Grønlund 和 Seth Pettie 在2014年从 3SUM 上削掉了对数因子，所以现在的猜想只要求不存在多项式级的改进。<bookmark mark='d'/>对工程师来说，条件下界是一条停止规则：别再找更好的指数了，去优化常数、并行或近似吧。

2575646c62bb.en: Some NP-hard problems are easy when a parameter is small. <bookmark mark='a'/> Vertex cover asks for k vertices touching every edge. Pick any edge; one of its ends must be in the cover. Branch on the two choices, and recurse with k minus one. The tree has at most two to the k plus one nodes. <bookmark mark='b'/> On our graphs of forty vertices, a cover of size twelve took under eight thousand nodes and eight milliseconds; trying every set of twelve vertices would mean five and a half billion. <bookmark mark='c'/> Jonathan Buss added a preprocessing rule: a vertex with more than k neighbours must be in any small cover, and after taking those, a yes-instance has at most k squared edges left. <bookmark mark='d'/> So every instance shrinks to a kernel of size polynomial in k before the search begins.
2575646c62bb.zh: 有些 NP 难问题在某个参数很小时是容易的。<bookmark mark='a'/>顶点覆盖要找 k 个顶点碰到每条边。任取一条边；它的两端之一必在覆盖中。对这两种选择分支，再以 k 减一递归。这棵树至多有二的 k 加一次方个节点。<bookmark mark='b'/>在我们四十个顶点的图上，规模为十二的覆盖用了不到八千个节点、八毫秒；尝试每个十二顶点的集合则意味着五十五亿个。<bookmark mark='c'/>Jonathan Buss 加了一条预处理规则：邻居多于 k 个的顶点必在任何小覆盖中，取走这些之后，一个“是”实例至多剩下 k 平方条边。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以在搜索开始之前，每个实例都缩成一个规模为 k 的多项式的核。

fc2f41f76af2.en: This is the theory of fixed-parameter tractability, built by Rodney Downey and Michael Fellows. <bookmark mark='a'/> A problem is FPT if it can be solved in time f of k times a polynomial in n, for any function f. <bookmark mark='b'/> Vertex cover is FPT; the record is about one point two seven to the k. <bookmark mark='c'/> Clique, by contrast, is W-one-hard: it is believed to need n to the k. <bookmark mark='d'/> A different parameter, treewidth, measures how much a graph resembles a tree. <bookmark mark='e'/> Bruno Courcelle proved that any property expressible in monadic second-order logic can be checked in linear time on graphs of bounded treewidth. <bookmark mark='f'/> Colouring, Hamiltonian cycles and independent sets all become easy on such graphs, which include many real networks.
fc2f41f76af2.zh: 这就是固定参数可解性的理论，由 Rodney Downey 和 Michael Fellows 建立。<bookmark mark='a'/>如果一个问题能在 f(k) 乘以 n 的多项式的时间内解决，f 是任意函数，它就是 FPT 的。<bookmark mark='b'/>顶点覆盖是 FPT 的；纪录大约是一点二七的 k 次方。<bookmark mark='c'/>相比之下，团问题是 W[1] 难的：人们相信它需要 n 的 k 次方。<bookmark mark='d'/>另一个参数，树宽，衡量一个图有多像树。<bookmark mark='e'/>Bruno Courcelle 证明，任何能用一元二阶逻辑表达的性质，在树宽有界的图上都能在线性时间内检查。<bookmark mark='f'/>着色、哈密顿圈和独立集，在这类图上都变得容易，而许多真实网络就属于这类图。

4ee69d28d363.en: NP asks whether a certificate exists. <bookmark mark='a'/> Leslie Valiant defined the class sharp-P in 1979: count the certificates. <bookmark mark='b'/> How many assignments satisfy this formula? Chapter six's sum-check protocol was exactly such a count. <bookmark mark='c'/> Here are two famous functions of a matrix. They differ only by a sign. <bookmark mark='d'/> The determinant, with the signs, is computed by Gaussian elimination in cubic time. <bookmark mark='e'/> The permanent, without them, counts the perfect matchings of a bipartite graph when the matrix has zeros and ones. <bookmark mark='f'/> Valiant proved the permanent sharp-P-complete. Finding one perfect matching is easy, as Part 18 showed; counting them is as hard as counting the solutions of any NP problem.
4ee69d28d363.zh: NP 问的是证书是否存在。<bookmark mark='a'/>Leslie Valiant 在1979年定义了 #P 类：数出证书的个数。<bookmark mark='b'/>有多少个赋值满足这个公式？第6章的 sum-check 协议正是这样的计数。<bookmark mark='c'/>这是矩阵的两个著名函数。它们只差一个符号。<bookmark mark='d'/>带符号的行列式，用高斯消元在立方时间内算出。<bookmark mark='e'/>不带符号的积和式，当矩阵只含零和一时，数的是一个二部图的完美匹配。<bookmark mark='f'/>Valiant 证明积和式是 #P 完全的。找到一个完美匹配很容易，正如第18部分所示；数出它们则和数任何 NP 问题的解一样难。

2bf8f510954a.en: We timed both on random zero-one matrices, with exact integers. <bookmark mark='a'/> The best known algorithm for the permanent is still Herbert Ryser's from 1963: inclusion and exclusion over subsets of columns, about two to the n steps. <bookmark mark='b'/> At n equals twenty, our matrix has over two trillion perfect matchings, and counting them took two point three seconds. <bookmark mark='c'/> The determinant of the same matrix took a quarter of a millisecond, and a two-hundred by two-hundred determinant takes under a second. <bookmark mark='d'/> Every two extra rows multiply the permanent's time by about four. One sign separates polynomial from exponential.
2bf8f510954a.zh: 我们在随机零一矩阵上用精确整数给两者计时。<bookmark mark='a'/>已知最好的积和式算法仍是 Herbert Ryser 1963年的：对列的子集做容斥，大约二的 n 次方步。<bookmark mark='b'/>n 等于二十时，我们的矩阵有超过两万亿个完美匹配，数完用了二点三秒。<bookmark mark='c'/>同一个矩阵的行列式用了四分之一毫秒，而二百乘二百的行列式不到一秒。<bookmark mark='d'/>每多两行，积和式的时间约乘以四。一个符号，隔开了多项式与指数。

b9c13efb35e7.en: How much power does counting give? <bookmark mark='a'/> Seinosuke Toda proved in 1991 that a machine with a sharp-P oracle can decide everything in the polynomial hierarchy of Part 26. One count is worth any number of alternating quantifiers. <bookmark mark='b'/> Leslie Valiant and Vijay Vazirani showed that random constraints can isolate a single solution, so even deciding satisfiability for formulas promised to have at most one solution is hard. <bookmark mark='c'/> Approximate counting is much weaker: Larry Stockmeyer showed it needs only an NP oracle and randomness. <bookmark mark='d'/> And for the permanent of a non-negative matrix, Mark Jerrum, Alistair Sinclair and Eric Vigoda found a polynomial-time approximation in 2004, <bookmark mark='e'/> using a Markov chain that samples random matchings, the Markov chain Monte Carlo of AI, Built, Part 5. <bookmark mark='f'/> And one exact special case: Pieter Kasteleyn counted the perfect matchings of planar graphs in 1961, by turning the permanent into a determinant with cleverly chosen signs.
b9c13efb35e7.zh: 计数能给出多大的能力？<bookmark mark='a'/>户田诚之助在1991年证明，带 #P 预言机的机器能判定第26部分多项式层级中的一切。一次计数抵得上任意多层交替量词。<bookmark mark='b'/>Leslie Valiant 和 Vijay Vazirani 证明，随机约束可以隔离出单个解，所以即使对承诺至多有一个解的公式，判定可满足性也是难的。<bookmark mark='c'/>近似计数弱得多：Larry Stockmeyer 证明它只需要一个 NP 预言机加上随机性。<bookmark mark='d'/>而对非负矩阵的积和式，Mark Jerrum、Alistair Sinclair 和 Eric Vigoda 在2004年找到了多项式时间的近似，<bookmark mark='e'/>用的是一条对随机匹配采样的马尔可夫链，正是人工智能，从零搭建第5部分的马尔可夫链蒙特卡罗。<bookmark mark='f'/>还有一个精确的特例：Pieter Kasteleyn 在1961年数出了平面图的完美匹配，办法是巧妙地选择符号，把积和式变成行列式。

f8b80b190ea5.en: Chapter fourteen. Average case, and one-way functions.
f8b80b190ea5.zh: 第14章。平均情形与单向函数。

526126e70689.en: NP-completeness is about the worst case. Cryptography needs problems that are hard on random instances. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is the favourite test case. Take a random graph on a thousand vertices, and secretly add all the edges among k of them. <bookmark mark='b'/> A random graph already has cliques of about twice log n vertices, here about twenty. <bookmark mark='c'/> So once k is above twenty, the hidden clique is the only one that large, and trying every set of vertices would find it. <bookmark mark='d'/> A polynomial algorithm, taking the vertices of highest degree and cleaning up, finds nothing below seventy, and every clique from eighty on, near the square root of n log n. <bookmark mark='e'/> Spectral methods improve the constant, to any multiple of root n, but nobody knows a polynomial algorithm below that. <bookmark mark='f'/> The conjecture that none exists is now used as an assumption, like SETH, to explain why problems in statistics and machine learning have the same gap.
526126e70689.zh: NP 完全性说的是最坏情况。密码学需要在随机实例上就难的问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是最受欢迎的测试案例。取一个一千个顶点的随机图，偷偷把其中 k 个顶点之间的边全部加上。<bookmark mark='b'/>随机图本身就有约两倍 log n 个顶点的团，这里大约二十。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以 k 一旦超过二十，藏起来的团就是唯一那么大的团，尝试每个顶点集合就能找到它。<bookmark mark='d'/>一个多项式算法，取度数最高的顶点再清理一下，在七十以下什么也找不到，从八十起每个团都能找到，接近 n log n 的平方根。<bookmark mark='e'/>谱方法改进了常数，可以到根号 n 的任意倍数，但在那之下没人知道多项式算法。<bookmark mark='f'/>“不存在这样的算法”这个猜想，如今像 SETH 一样被当作假设，用来解释统计和机器学习中的问题为什么有同样的间隙。

5f8192fc8611.en: Cryptography needs something stronger: a function that is easy to compute and hard to invert on random inputs. <bookmark mark='a'/> Multiplication is the classic candidate. <bookmark mark='b'/> Multiplying two forty-bit primes takes about fifty nanoseconds. Factoring their product with Pollard's rho method took half a second. <bookmark mark='c'/> Rho needs about the fourth root of N steps, so every eight more bits cost about four times as much. <bookmark mark='d'/> The best known method, the number field sieve, is faster, but still worse than polynomial: the 829-bit challenge number RSA-250 fell in 2020, after about two thousand seven hundred core-years. <bookmark mark='e'/> Yet nobody has proved any function one-way. A proof would imply P is not NP.
5f8192fc8611.zh: 密码学需要更强的东西：一个容易计算、却在随机输入上难以求逆的函数。<bookmark mark='a'/>乘法是经典的候选。<bookmark mark='b'/>把两个四十位的素数相乘，大约五十纳秒。用 Pollard 的 rho 方法分解它们的乘积，用了半秒。<bookmark mark='c'/>Rho 大约需要 N 的四次方根步，所以每多八位，代价约乘以四。<bookmark mark='d'/>已知最好的方法，数域筛法，更快，但仍比多项式差：829位的挑战数 RSA-250 在2020年被攻破，用了大约两千七百个核年。<bookmark mark='e'/>然而没人证明过任何函数是单向的。这样的证明会推出 P 不等于 NP。

1c67bfc0cd96.en: This is the bridge to the next acts of the series. <bookmark mark='a'/> Leonid Levin started a theory of average-case completeness in 1986. <bookmark mark='b'/> Johan Håstad, Russell Impagliazzo, Levin and Michael Luby proved that any one-way function at all can be turned into a pseudorandom generator. <bookmark mark='c'/> From those come private-key encryption, signatures and the commitments of chapter seven: Impagliazzo's Minicrypt. Part 29 builds it. <bookmark mark='d'/> Miklós Ajtai found problems on lattices whose random instances are as hard as their worst ones, <bookmark mark='e'/> and Oded Regev's learning with errors turned that into public-key encryption that resists quantum computers, now standardized, in Part 30. <bookmark mark='f'/> What nobody can do is base cryptography on an NP-complete problem: results of Joan Feigenbaum and Lance Fortnow, and of Andrej Bogdanov and Luca Trevisan, suggest the standard techniques cannot.
1c67bfc0cd96.zh: 这是通向本系列下几幕的桥梁。<bookmark mark='a'/>Levin 在1986年开创了平均情形完全性的理论。<bookmark mark='b'/>Håstad、Impagliazzo、Levin 和 Luby 四人证明，任何一个单向函数，不论是什么样的，都能变成伪随机生成器。<bookmark mark='c'/>由此得到私钥加密、数字签名，以及第7章用过的承诺：这就是 Impagliazzo 所说的迷你密码国。第29部分会把它建起来。<bookmark mark='d'/>Ajtai 找到了格上的问题，它们的随机实例和最坏实例一样难，<bookmark mark='e'/>而 Regev 的带误差学习问题把这一点变成了能抵御量子计算机的公钥加密，如今已经成为标准，见第30部分。<bookmark mark='f'/>没有人能做到的，是把密码学建立在一个 NP 完全问题之上：Feigenbaum 与 Fortnow 的结果，以及 Bogdanov 与 Trevisan 的结果都表明，标准的技术做不到这一点。

734bbd65b2a7.en: Chapter fifteen. The frontier: MIP star equals RE, and proofs in practice.
734bbd65b2a7.zh: 第15章。前沿：MIP* 等于 RE，以及实践中的证明。

af7783e9eeaa.en: Each new kind of verifier has reached a larger class. <bookmark mark='a'/> Reading a proof gives NP. <bookmark mark='b'/> Questioning one prover with random coins gives PSPACE, chapter six's theorem. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 1988 Michael Ben-Or, Shafi Goldwasser, Joe Kilian and Avi Wigderson asked: what if there are two provers, questioned separately, like suspects in different rooms? László Babai, Lance Fortnow and Carsten Lund showed in 1991 that this reaches nondeterministic exponential time. It was the seed of the PCP theorem. <bookmark mark='d'/> Then the provers were allowed to share quantum entanglement. In 2020 Zhengfeng Ji, Anand Natarajan, Thomas Vidick, John Wright and Henry Yuen proved that the class jumps all the way to RE. <bookmark mark='e'/> A verifier who runs in polynomial time can be convinced that a program halts, a question no algorithm can decide.
af7783e9eeaa.zh: 每一种新的验证者，都到达了一个更大的类。<bookmark mark='a'/>只读一份证明，得到的是 NP。<bookmark mark='b'/>用随机硬币向一个证明者提问，得到的是 PSPACE，这是第6章的定理。<bookmark mark='c'/>1988年，Ben-Or、Goldwasser、Kilian 和 Wigderson 四人问：如果有两个证明者，分开审问，就像关在不同房间里的两个嫌疑人，又会怎样？Babai、Fortnow 和 Lund 在1991年证明，这样能到达非确定指数时间。它是 PCP 定理的种子。<bookmark mark='d'/>后来，又允许这两个证明者共享量子纠缠。2020年，季铮锋、Natarajan、Vidick、Wright 和袁浩森五人证明，这个类一路跳到了 RE。<bookmark mark='e'/>一个只在多项式时间里运行的验证者，竟然可以被说服相信某个程序会停机，而这是任何算法都无法判定的问题。

9015b12fbf04.en: The result reached far beyond complexity theory. <bookmark mark='a'/> The verifier tests whether the provers' answers show correlations that only entanglement can produce, the kind of Bell test Part 53 describes. <bookmark mark='b'/> Entanglement helps honest provers, but it also helps cheaters, which is what makes these games hard to analyse. <bookmark mark='c'/> The key step compresses verifiers: a game that checks a larger game, which checks a larger one, so that a finite conversation certifies an unbounded computation. <bookmark mark='d'/> As a consequence, Tsirelson's problem in physics has a negative answer: two natural mathematical models of quantum correlations are different. <bookmark mark='e'/> And Alain Connes's embedding conjecture of 1976, a central question about operator algebras, is false. <bookmark mark='f'/> A long proof about interactive proofs settled a problem in pure mathematics.
9015b12fbf04.zh: 这个结果的影响远远超出了复杂性理论。<bookmark mark='a'/>验证者检验证明者的回答是否呈现只有纠缠才能产生的关联，也就是第53部分描述的那种贝尔测试。<bookmark mark='b'/>纠缠帮助诚实的证明者，但也帮助作弊者，这正是这类博弈难以分析的原因。<bookmark mark='c'/>关键一步是压缩验证者：一个博弈检查一个更大的博弈，后者又检查一个更大的，于是一场有限的对话就能为一个无界的计算作证。<bookmark mark='d'/>作为推论，物理学中的 Tsirelson 问题答案是否定的：量子关联的两种自然数学模型是不同的。<bookmark mark='e'/>而 Alain Connes 1976年的嵌入猜想，算子代数中的一个核心问题，是错的。<bookmark mark='f'/>一篇关于交互式证明的长篇证明，解决了纯数学中的一个问题。

5fd5ad17e323.en: Meanwhile, interactive proofs went into production. <bookmark mark='a'/> The recipe: write a computation as a circuit, turn the circuit into polynomials, check them with sum-check or a PCP, commit to the polynomials cryptographically, and replace the verifier's random coins with a hash of the transcript, the trick of Amos Fiat and Adi Shamir. <bookmark mark='b'/> The result is a proof of a few hundred bytes that anyone can check in milliseconds, however long the computation was. <bookmark mark='c'/> Joe Kilian and Silvio Micali saw this in the 1990s; Goldwasser, Kalai and Rothblum built delegation on sum-check in 2008. <bookmark mark='d'/> Jens Groth's 2016 system needs just three group elements, and Zcash used such proofs the same year for private payments. <bookmark mark='e'/> Rollups execute thousands of transactions elsewhere and post one proof. <bookmark mark='f'/> Zero-knowledge virtual machines prove that an entire RISC-V program ran correctly. <bookmark mark='g'/> The catch is the prover, still orders of magnitude slower than simply running the program; making it fast is an active race.
5fd5ad17e323.zh: 与此同时，交互式证明投入了生产。<bookmark mark='a'/>配方是：把计算写成电路，把电路变成多项式，用 sum-check 或 PCP 检查它们，用密码学方法对多项式做承诺，再用对话记录的哈希代替验证者的随机硬币，这是 Amos Fiat 和 Adi Shamir 的技巧。<bookmark mark='b'/>结果是一份几百字节的证明，任何人都能在几毫秒内检查，不论那个计算有多长。<bookmark mark='c'/>Joe Kilian 和 Silvio Micali 在1990年代看到了这一点；Goldwasser、Kalai 和 Rothblum 在2008年把委托计算建立在 sum-check 之上。<bookmark mark='d'/>Jens Groth 2016年的系统只需要三个群元素，Zcash 同年就用这样的证明做隐私支付。<bookmark mark='e'/>Rollup 在别处执行成千上万笔交易，只上传一份证明。<bookmark mark='f'/>零知识虚拟机证明一个完整的 RISC-V 程序被正确执行。<bookmark mark='g'/>代价在证明者那一方，它仍比直接运行程序慢好几个数量级；让它变快，是一场正在进行的竞赛。

b1cd5b0fa044.en: Six open problems. <bookmark mark='a'/> Whether randomness ever helps polynomial-time computation, and whether that can be shown without first proving circuit lower bounds, which Kabanets and Impagliazzo showed is nearly unavoidable. <bookmark mark='b'/> Whether the Unique Games Conjecture is true. <bookmark mark='c'/> How the three fine-grained conjectures relate: no reduction between any two is known. <bookmark mark='d'/> Valiant's algebraic version of P versus NP: does the permanent need algebraic circuits of superpolynomial size? <bookmark mark='e'/> Whether cryptography can rest on an NP-complete problem. <bookmark mark='f'/> And how sound the simplest tests can be: the exact rejection curve of the linearity test, whose start we measured in chapter eight. <bookmark mark='g'/> This part's research problem takes a small, computable case of the sixth.
b1cd5b0fa044.zh: 六个未解问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>随机性是否曾经帮助多项式时间计算，以及能否不先证明电路下界就证明这一点，Kabanets 和 Impagliazzo 证明这几乎无法回避。<bookmark mark='b'/>唯一博弈猜想是否成立。<bookmark mark='c'/>三个细粒度猜想之间是什么关系：任何两个之间都不知道有归约。<bookmark mark='d'/>Valiant 的代数版 P 与 NP：积和式是否需要超多项式规模的代数电路？<bookmark mark='e'/>密码学能否建立在 NP 完全问题之上。<bookmark mark='f'/>以及最简单的测试能有多可靠：线性性测试的精确拒绝曲线，我们在第8章测量了它的开头。<bookmark mark='g'/>这一部分的研究题取第六个问题的一个小而可计算的情形。

de7e5e5c0976.en: What we built in this part. Randomized classes, amplification and Adleman's theorem in numbers; pseudorandomness from hardness. Random restrictions collapsing a formula, and the communication cost of equality. Interactive proofs, and sum-check run step by step, catching a cheater at the predicted rate. Zero knowledge, with a simulator nobody can tell from the real thing. The PCP theorem, the linearity test, and why a coin is the best approximation for MAX-3SAT; the Unique Games Conjecture. Fine-grained and parameterized complexity, counting, and the average case that cryptography needs.
de7e5e5c0976.zh: 这一部分我们搭建了什么。随机复杂性类，放大，以及用数字呈现的 Adleman 定理；由困难得到的伪随机性。让公式塌缩的随机限制，以及相等问题的通信代价。交互式证明，以及逐步运行的 sum-check，以预测的概率抓住作弊者。零知识，配一个谁也分辨不出真假的模拟器。PCP 定理、线性性测试，以及为什么硬币是 MAX-3SAT 的最佳近似；唯一博弈猜想。细粒度复杂性与参数化复杂性，计数，以及密码学所需要的平均情形。

434542f06295.en: Where this comes back. Part 28 builds the codes that PCPs are made of: Reed-Solomon, which is polynomial evaluation, and codes you can test by reading a few symbols. Part 29 builds pseudorandom generators from one-way functions. Part 30 turns zero knowledge into signatures with Fiat and Shamir, builds public keys on lattices, and sketches succinct proofs. Part 53 meets entanglement and the game behind MIP star. Part 56 builds expanders, the engine of Dinur's proof. And Part 57 shows why some learning problems are hard, using cryptographic assumptions like those of chapter fourteen.
434542f06295.zh: 这些内容在哪里再次出现。第28部分搭建构成 PCP 的编码：Reed-Solomon，它就是多项式求值，以及只读几个符号就能检验的编码。第29部分从单向函数搭建伪随机生成器。第30部分用 Fiat 和 Shamir 的办法把零知识变成签名，在格上搭建公钥，并概述简洁证明。第53部分会遇到纠缠，以及 MIP* 背后的那个博弈。第56部分搭建扩展图，Dinur 证明的引擎。而第57部分用类似第14章的密码学假设，说明为什么有些学习问题是难的。

eea8bbe185df.en: In practice. Compare huge files by fingerprints, a few dozen bits instead of all of them. Use succinct proofs to check computations you did not run yourself. Use zero knowledge to prove you know a secret without revealing it. Treat a conditional lower bound as a stopping rule. And when a hard problem has a small parameter, shrink the instance to a kernel and search.
eea8bbe185df.zh: 实践中。用指纹比较巨大的文件，只要几十位而不是全部。用简洁证明检查你没有亲自运行的计算。用零知识证明你知道一个秘密而不泄露它。把条件下界当作停止规则。而当一个难题有一个小参数时，先把实例缩成核，再去搜索。

436deb9a4797.en: Six problems, with full solutions in the part's notes. Pause on any of them. The fifth is a build problem: a non-interactive sum-check proof with the Fiat-Shamir transform. The last, marked with a star, is a research problem: its general answer is not known, and the notes say where to start.
436deb9a4797.zh: 六道习题，完整解答在本部分的笔记里。可以在任何一题上暂停。第五题是动手题：用 Fiat-Shamir 变换做一个非交互的 sum-check 证明。最后一题标了星号，是研究题：它的一般答案还不知道，笔记里写了从哪里入手。

7db4fe070dde.en: Next time: errors. In 1947 Richard Hamming's weekend jobs kept dying on bad bits, so he taught the machine to fix them. Polynomials, the same ones that powered sum-check, become codes that survive scratches. Claude Shannon proved how much noise costs, and it took fifty years to reach his limit. We will scratch a QR code and recover its message. Part 28, Error-Correcting Codes.
7db4fe070dde.zh: 下一次：错误。1947年，Richard Hamming 的周末作业总因坏位而死掉，于是他教机器去纠正它们。多项式，正是驱动 sum-check 的那些，变成了能经受划痕的编码。Claude Shannon 证明了噪声的代价有多大，而人们花了五十年才达到他的极限。我们会划花一个二维码，再把它的信息找回来。第28部分，纠错码。

9bd24692775d.en: The books and papers this part follows are on screen and in the notes. Thank you for watching.
9bd24692775d.zh: 这一部分所依据的书籍和论文都在屏幕上和笔记里。感谢观看。
